title: WPSS/3910/2018 of SMT. CHANDRA DEVI Vs UNION OF INDIA THROUGH SECRETARY MINISTRY OF DEFENCE NEW DELHI

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No. 3910 of 2018
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 Mr. T.P.S. Takuli, Advocate, for the
petitioner.
Mrs. Monika Pant, Standing Counsel for the
Union of India.
Being conscious of the fact, that the
petitioner, who happens to be a senior citizen,
claims the retiral benefits and the grant of the
family pension, which according to her was
admissible to be paid to her late husband Shri Hayat
Singh. Late Mr. Hayat Singh was a member of the
Indian Armed Forces, and at the time, when he was
inducted into the Armed Forces, he had married one
Smt. Dharma Devi, in 1945. It is said that Mrs.
Dharma Devi, whose whereabouts were not known
and since she was not discharging her matrimonial
obligation, qua late Mr. Hayat Singh, the second
marriage was solemnized with the petitioner, by her
late husband Mr. Hayat Singh on 20th
 June, 1956.
Mr. Hayat Singh, met with the sad demise on 12th
June, 2016, after having retired from the Armed
Forces in the year 1968.
The prayer in the present Writ Petition,
which has been prayed for by the petitioner, is
extracted hereunder :-
"I. Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the respondents to
pay/release the family pension to the petitioner
forthwith, otherwise the petitioner shall suffer
irreparable loss and injury and the same cannot be
compensated by any means.
II. Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the respondents to
give the due pension from June, 2016 alongwith
applicable interest forthwith to the petitioner.
III. Issue any other order or direction which
this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the
circumstances of the case.

IV. Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of Certiorari quashing the impugned order
dated 30.06.2018 passed by respondent no.3, by
which the claim of the petitioner for family pension
has been rejected (annexure no.4 to the counter
affidavit.)"
Since despite of the fact, that she being the
second wife, since there was no statutory bar
because the Hindu Marriage Act, was enforced
subsequent to the second marriage, she would still
be entitled to be granted the retiral benefits and the
family pension as admissible to her as a
consequence of the death of late Mr. Hayat Singh.
Learned counsel for the petitioner had made
reference to a Government Order No. G0-
02/769/Das-917-61 dated 24th August, 1966, which
related to its applicability on the subject called as
'New Pension Scheme of 1965' and in terms of the
parameters which had been laid down therein, in the
said Government Order, he intended to argue that in
fact, there is no bar created under law for the
purposes of determination of the retiral benefits, to
the second wife, who had solemnized the marriage
prior to the enforcement of the Hindu Marriage Act.
In fact, I am of the view, that since the late
Mr. Hayat Singh, husband of the petitioner, was
member of the Armed Services and was a Central
Government employee, the parameters governing
the determination of the family pension under the
Scheme of 1965, as applicable to the State
Government employees, under the prevalent State
laws, since constituting to be the part of the U.P.
Retirement Benefit Rules of 1961, the same would
not governed the terms and the service conditions
of the employees of the Armed Forces. Hence,
this Government Order of 24th
 August, 1966,
would not be applicable, in the circumstances of
the present case.
The petitioner's contention, that the first wife
Dharma Devi, whose whereabouts were not known,
since she was not having any issues out of later Mr.
Hayat Singh, and rather, in fact, she claims, that she
would be the only surviving heirs and in support
thereto, the learned counsel for the petitioner makes

reference to the family register, that all the
offsprings were born out of the second wedlock of
late Mr. Hayat Singh, with the present petitioner.
This aspect about the heirship of late Mr. Hayat
Singh, whether they are the offsprings from the first
wife or the second wife, and their respective
entitlement on the family pension and retiral
benefits of the armed personnel could only be
decided, when the succession rights are determined
by the competent Civil Courts, about the
entitlement to receive the benefits, which late Mr.
Hayat Singh, would otherwise be entitled to receive
on attainment of age of superannuation in 1968.
This determination requires a factual appreciation
and determination of evidence of the entitlement of
the petitioner to receive the benefits, which cannot
be decided by the Writ Courts under Article 226 of
the Constitution of India.
 In that eventuality, this Writ Petition is
dismissed with the liberty left open to the petitioner
to seek an appropriate remedy, for declaration of
her rights qua the assets of late Mr. Hayat Singh
and the consequential benefits, which could have
flown to her in accordance with the law by
approaching the Civil Court
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Dated 15.12.2021
Shiv
